newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU Court advisor backs UK line on cigarette tax.
newsitem.headline: EU Court advisor backs UK line on cigarette tax.

text.p: The European Court of Justice's chief legal advisor backed on Thursday Britain's argument that cigarettes bought in Luxembourg and shipped to Britain should be subject to full British excise tax.

The legal opinion by Advocate General Damaso Ruiz-Jarabo Colombo, which is subject to approval by the full court, is a blow to The Enlightened Tobacco Company, which used a tax loophole to sell cut-price cigarettes in Britain.
The firm operated a scheme to buy cigarettes through its subsidiary, EMU Tabac in Luxembourg, for resale through The Man in Black intermediary, another ETC subsidiary.
Customers order up to four cartons of cigarettes, each containing 200, which are shipped to them direct by the agent.
British tax authorities seized some of the cigarettes and required the payment of excise duty to release the goods.

Enlightened Tobacco hoped the court would take the position that EU rules allowing private individuals to buy and transport small quantities of goods between member states would apply to purchases made through a consumer agent.
The court's advocate general said the concept of purchase by an individual precludes any role for an intermediary in the purchase or transport of the goods.
Rulings by the court itself, in this case scheduled for some later this year, usually follow the line argued by the Advovate General.
